advice: Propose a bounded transpose-fusion experiment in the active panel32 path. For each 32-row A band, transpose a small K-by-row tile into a temporary buffer, then feed that tile to the existing FP32 FMOPA loop before writing it to the full 64 KiB scratch panel. Keep the current column-panel traversal and accumulation order. Process all 512 K values exactly once per row band; do not recompute the transpose for each output-column panel. Count tile-buffer writes and reads, full-panel writes and reads, and any added allocation or pointer work inside gemm. Compare against the exact eb091b1e source and unchanged paired controls. This tests whether fusing transpose with consumption can remove full-panel traffic; it is unmeasured advice, not a performance claim.
risks: Fusion may require restructuring the active assembly and stack use, may increase SME transitions or register pressure, and may simply move rather than remove data movement. A design that repeats transpose work for each of the 16 output-column panels would add 15 redundant transposes per A band and should be rejected. Preserve row-major C=A@B, FP32 update order, general-size fallback, ABI state, 64-byte stack alignment, bounds, and all license text. Validate fresh inputs, full output overwrite, input preservation, all 48 public cases including tails and n<=0, and the existing 0.002 tolerance. Then use the fixed ten-run validation and paired-control gates without changing power settings; compare historical and fresh same-mode peaks separately.
